games.name: Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup
games.info:
**Context:** A late character may have a rare combination of god, mutations, skills, equipment, and rune progress, all erased by one death.

**How progress is saved:** Local characters are saved for continuation, but the normal roguelike flow has no reusable manual rollback points.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a rune branch, vault, Abyss trip, or other high-risk push. Restore the same character after a tactical mistake instead of starting from a new seed.

games.name: NetHack
games.info:
**Context:** A strong character can represent hours of equipment, intrinsics, identification knowledge, and dungeon progress, all lost on one death.

**How progress is saved:** Saving is suspend-and-resume: loading consumes the save instead of leaving a reusable rollback point.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a dangerous branch, vault, wish experiment, or ascension push. A restore lets you retry the same character instead of rebuilding the run from scratch.

games.name: ScourgeBringer
games.info:
**Context:** A strong run can have a valuable combination of blessings, items, health, and upgrades before a difficult boss or region.

**How progress is saved:** Save & Exit provides a clean run-save boundary; arbitrary live combat state should not be assumed to be on disk.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint at Save & Exit before a boss or new area. Restore the same build after failure instead of rerolling another run.

games.name: Terraria
games.info:
**Context:** Hardcore is mostly an optional challenge, but it is specifically required for the **Extra Life** achievement.

**How progress is saved:** Character and world saves are separate, so checkpoint both when you want a clean pre-attempt rollback.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before the **Extra Life** attempt or another high-risk Hardcore milestone. If the character is lost or the attempt goes wrong, restore instead of rebuilding the geared Hardcore character.

games.name: Signs of the Sojourner
games.info:
**Context:** One conversation can change the deck you carry into every later relationship, sometimes locking you out of future dialogue paths.

**How progress is saved:** The game uses a single local save rather than manual branch slots.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before an important conversation or route stop. Restore if the resulting card changes or relationship outcome damages the deck/path you were aiming for.

games.name: Jagged Alliance 3
games.info:
**Context:** The **Ironman** achievement requires the harshest campaign settings, including Dead is Dead and To The Bitter End.

**How progress is saved:** Those settings heavily restrict rollback and can autosave around tactical actions, so the exact captured state matters.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before storming a fortified sector, boss encounter, or fight where a favorite merc can die. Restore after a disastrous engagement instead of restarting the full Ironman challenge.

games.name: Project Zomboid
games.info:
**Context:** A mature survivor and Knox Country world can contain months of skills, bases, vehicles, crops, generators, and carefully moved loot.

**How progress is saved:** The survivor and persistent world are saved together continuously rather than through manual slots, so a useful rollback must restore the matching save state.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before Louisville runs, clearing dense buildings, moving loaded vehicles, or continuing after a suspicious bite. Restore both character and world after a fatal mistake.

games.name: Baldur's Gate 3
games.info:
**Context:** Completing Honour Mode awards **Foehammer**, but a party wipe can end eligibility after dozens of hours.

**How progress is saved:** Honour Mode keeps a single campaign save, so there is no normal earlier save to return to after a disaster.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a dangerous boss, high-stakes dialogue, or other run-ending situation. Restore after a wipe instead of restarting the entire Foehammer attempt.

games.name: Monster Train
games.info:
**Context:** A late deck may depend on a very specific clan, unit-upgrade, artifact, removal, and spell package.

**How progress is saved:** The campaign is saved on the world map; combat is not normally serialized turn-by-turn and usually restarts as a whole.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a merchant, banner, artifact choice, or difficult ring. Restore to compare build decisions or retry from the pre-combat state, not individual combat turns.

games.name: Yes, Your Grace
games.info:
**Context:** A choice made many days earlier can decide alliances, family outcomes, resources, or the war, but the game only keeps a short rolling history.

**How progress is saved:** Only the most recent eight day-end saves are retained.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint a pivotal day before a major alliance, family decision, or resource commitment. Return to it later even after the built-in eight-day history has rolled past.

games.name: Revita
games.info:
**Context:** A strong climb can depend on a delicate relic synergy and health-for-upgrade trades before the next tower section or secret-boss route.

**How progress is saved:** Save & Quit is available at terminals after bosses rather than at arbitrary rooms.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint at the post-boss terminal. Restore the same relic/health build after the next section fails instead of rebuilding it from the first station.

games.name: Shiren the Wanderer: The Tower of Fortune and the Dice of Fate
games.info:
**Context:** A failed dungeon expedition can cost upgraded weapons, shields, bracelets, consumables, money, and the current dungeon position.

**How progress is saved:** Suspend preserves an expedition for continuation, not as a set of earlier dungeon checkpoints.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before pushing deeper with valuable upgraded gear. If a floor, trap chain, or boss kills the run, restore the same loadout instead of rebuilding it.

games.name: Gears Tactics
games.info:
**Context:** The **I am Ironman** achievement requires completing the campaign with Ironman enabled.

**How progress is saved:** Ironman removes normal manual rollback and commits campaign progress through autosaves.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a difficult mission or fail-critical hero deployment. Restore after a disastrous turn or mission loss instead of replaying the campaign for the achievement.

games.name: Pentiment
games.info:
**Context:** Major investigation and dialogue choices are mutually exclusive and can change later acts.

**How progress is saved:** Choices are committed through autosaves rather than user-managed save slots.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint immediately before an accusation, investigation commitment, or major dialogue branch. Take one outcome, then restore and follow the other branch without replaying the act.

games.name: Suzerain
games.info:
**Context:** Constitution, economy, alliances, cabinet choices, and endings branch from decisions that may only show their consequences hours later.

**How progress is saved:** The campaign autosaves committed decisions instead of providing normal manual branch saves.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a constitutional vote, budget decision, privatization/nationalization choice, alliance, or cabinet crisis. Restore to pursue another outcome without replaying the presidency from the start.

games.name: The Life and Suffering of Sir Brante
games.info:
**Context:** Major life choices are mutually exclusive and can change family, career, romance, politics, and the ending several chapters later.

**How progress is saved:** The life is autosaved as choices are committed; there is no normal library of decision-point saves.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before an estate, family, romance, trial, or revolutionary branch. Take one outcome, then restore for another instead of replaying whole chapters.
installDirs: The Life and Suffering of Sir Brante

windows: The Life and Suffering of Sir Brante.exe

save.path: {HOME}/AppData/LocalLow/SEVER/The Life and Suffering of Sir Brante/Saves

games.name: Voidigo
games.info:
**Context:** A late run can carry a strong weapon, upgrades, boss rewards, and health state that disappears on death.

**How progress is saved:** The run can be saved in the Anti-Void between levels; that inter-level transition is the reliable checkpoint boundary.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint between stages before the next biome or boss. Restore the same build after death instead of rerolling its weapons and upgrades.

games.name: Risk of Rain Returns
games.info:
**Context:** The desired value is protecting a powerful item build before a late teleporter, Providence route, or difficult stage.

**How progress is saved:** The game does not provide normal Save & Quit for an active run.

**SaveScummer value:** A file-only SaveScummer cannot restore that live build, so the main use case remains unsupported without runtime capture.

games.name: HighFleet
games.info:
**Context:** A bad battle or route gamble can destroy irreplaceable ships, fuel, ammunition, and strategic position far from the last Fleet HQ checkpoint.

**How progress is saved:** The game provides campaign restore points at Fleet HQs rather than fine-grained manual rollback everywhere.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a strike-group battle, risky refit, fuel-critical route, or nuclear escalation. Restore without replaying the long stretch since the previous Fleet HQ.

games.name: Road 96
games.info:
**Context:** A single road trip can change recurring-character relationships, resources, border outcomes, and the wider campaign state.

**How progress is saved:** Campaign progress is autosaved rather than exposed as manual branch slots.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a pivotal encounter, border crossing, or expensive route choice. Restore to see another outcome without replaying several procedural legs to reach a similar point.

games.name: OTXO
games.info:
**Context:** A good mansion run can have a preferred gun set, drink upgrades, money, and room progress that took several floors to assemble.

**How progress is saved:** Save & Exit preserves the active run for continuation.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a difficult mansion section or boss. Restore the same loadout after a failed room sequence instead of rebuilding it from the start.

games.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters
games.info:
**Context:** The **Grand Master** achievement requires winning in Grand Master mode, where losses and strategic mistakes are committed.

**How progress is saved:** Grand Master uses a single campaign save instead of freely reloadable manual slots.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a difficult Bloom mission, boss, or deployment with veteran Knights. Restore after a roster-wrecking loss or strategic spiral instead of restarting the Grand Master run.

games.name: Star Trek: Infinite
games.info:
**Context:** Achievements require Ironman, so a long faction run can be lost to a bad war, mission-chain choice, or diplomatic commitment.

**How progress is saved:** Ironman disables manual saving and uses automatic saves; current versions can use local Ironman saves without requiring cloud saves.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a major war, faction mission choice, or diplomatic break. Restore after a run-derailing outcome without abandoning the achievement attempt.

games.name: Dome Keeper
games.info:
**Context:** A run can hinge on a particular gadget, upgrade path, mined resource haul, and defense setup.

**How progress is saved:** The active run is persisted for resume; checkpoints are safest around known exit/autosave boundaries.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before an expensive upgrade choice or a wave that will test the build. Restore to compare upgrade paths or retry the defense without replaying the whole mine.

games.name: XCOM: Enemy Unknown
games.info:
**Context:** The **No Looking Back** achievement requires beating the game in Ironman on Classic or Impossible.

**How progress is saved:** Ironman disables manual and multiple saves, committing tactical casualties and campaign state to one history.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a terror mission, base assault, or difficult UFO operation. Restore after a squad wipe or veteran loss instead of restarting the No Looking Back run.

games.name: Torchlight II
games.info:
**Context:** Several achievements are tied to Hardcore characters, where one death can erase a high-level build and its gear.

**How progress is saved:** Hardcore character progress is stored in local save data and death permanently ends that character.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before an act boss, Phase Beast challenge, or dangerous Mapworks run. Restore a dead achievement-run character instead of leveling and gearing another one from scratch.

games.name: Crusader Kings II
games.info:
**Context:** CK2 achievements are tied to Ironman-compatible campaigns, where a bad succession, ruler death, or war can undo decades of setup.

**How progress is saved:** Ironman continually overwrites one campaign save instead of keeping manual rollback slots.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a succession, faction revolt, risky war, imprisonment, or inheritance play. Restore the dynasty after a disastrous outcome without abandoning the achievement run.

games.name: FTL: Faster Than Light
games.info:
**Context:** A late ship can have a rare crew, weapon package, augments, systems, and damage state that took several sectors to assemble.

**How progress is saved:** FTL keeps one active-run continuation save that is overwritten as the run advances and disappears when the run ends.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a dangerous beacon, sector exit, or Flagship phase. Retry the same ship and strategy after a catastrophic fight instead of rebuilding the run.

games.name: Total War: Rome II
games.info:
**Context:** A Legendary campaign can lose veteran armies, provinces, and political stability to one bad war or civil conflict.

**How progress is saved:** Legendary restricts loading to the current/latest autosave rather than normal manual saves.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a decisive siege, civil-war risk, or major declaration. Restore the pre-war campaign instead of rebuilding armies and provinces over many turns.

games.name: Don't Starve
games.info:
**Context:** A single world can contain seasons of base building, resource networks, explored map, boss loot, and winter preparation, all lost if the survivor dies without resurrection.

**How progress is saved:** The current world is saved automatically; a terminal death ends that run rather than leaving a normal rollback slot.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a boss, winter expedition, cave trip, or other stretch where resurrection is uncertain. Restore the same base and world instead of generating and rebuilding a new one.

games.name: Grim Dawn
games.info:
**Context:** Grim Dawn has multiple Hardcore-only achievements, including high-level and Ultimate-difficulty goals that can take a long time to reach.

**How progress is saved:** Hardcore character progress is stored locally and death permanently ends the character.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a nemesis, roguelike dungeon, celestial boss, or deep Shattered Realm push. Restore the same achievement-run character after a death instead of rebuilding its level, devotion map, and gear.

games.name: Teleglitch: Die More Edition
games.info:
**Context:** A late run can be resource-starved but valuable, with a specific weapon, ammo, armor, and crafting setup.

**How progress is saved:** The game uses single-use exit saves at level boundaries; Steam builds need restore testing because cloud/API behavior can interfere with copied saves.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before loading into a dangerous later level. If the run dies, restore the same inventory and resource state instead of restarting, provided the platform-specific restore works.

games.name: Europa Universalis IV
games.info:
**Context:** EU4 achievements require Ironman, so an achievement run can represent centuries of setup that one war, succession, peace deal, or bad click can ruin.

**How progress is saved:** Ironman keeps one evolving campaign save and disables normal manual branching.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a major war, PU/succession play, peace deal, or achievement-critical decision. Restore the campaign without abandoning the Ironman achievement attempt.

games.name: The Banner Saga
games.info:
**Context:** Deaths, caravan decisions, supplies, and major story choices can carry forward into later games in the trilogy.

**How progress is saved:** The game autosaves at checkpoints rather than offering unrestricted branch saves.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a battle with possible hero loss or a major caravan/story decision. Restore to preserve a different import state for later games without replaying the whole journey.

games.name: Nuclear Throne
games.info:
**Context:** The desired use case is protecting a late mutant build with specific mutations, crown, weapons, and loop progress.

**How progress is saved:** The game does not normally save an active run for later continuation; local saves mainly cover persistent progression.

**SaveScummer value:** A file-only SaveScummer cannot restore the live run. Preserving a pre-Throne or loop checkpoint would require runtime capture rather than ordinary save-file versioning.

games.name: Invisible, Inc.
games.info:
**Context:** High-difficulty campaigns give only a limited number of Rewinds, so one alarm cascade or captured veteran can consume a scarce recovery resource.

**How progress is saved:** The campaign autosaves, while Rewind is the built-in limited rollback mechanism.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a high-security facility or after spending the last Rewind. Restore after a failed infiltration instead of losing a veteran agent or abandoning the campaign.

games.name: Crypt of the NecroDancer
games.info:
**Context:** Long Deathless, Story, or All-Characters sessions can represent substantial progress that one rhythm mistake can erase.

**How progress is saved:** Current versions can save and resume these sessions, giving SaveScummer a real serialized run state to version.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a difficult zone or boss sequence. Restore a long multi-character session after failure instead of repeating all earlier characters or zones.

games.name: Risk of Rain
games.info:
**Context:** The desired value is protecting a late survivor with a rare item stack before a teleporter, boss, or loop.

**How progress is saved:** The original game does not save active run progress for later continuation.

**SaveScummer value:** A file-only SaveScummer cannot preserve the live run; the attractive late-run rollback needs runtime capture.

games.name: NEO Scavenger
games.info:
**Context:** A viable survivor may depend on hard-won clothing, tools, medicine, shelter knowledge, and map progress, while one wound, infection, or bad encounter can end the run.

**How progress is saved:** The game keeps a single current survivor state rather than manual rollback slots.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before combat, risky scavenging, travel while injured, or an uncertain encounter. Restore a known-good survivor instead of rebuilding the entire survival setup.

games.name: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth
games.info:
**Context:** A rare item synergy or completion-mark run can be hard to reproduce once a late death ends it.

**How progress is saved:** An active run has continuation data for Continue, but the game does not keep a reusable history of earlier run states.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a late boss, sacrifice sequence, or route decision. Restore the exact build after failure instead of rerolling until the same synergy appears again.

games.name: Tales of Maj'Eyal
games.info:
**Context:** A high-level character can carry a specialized talent build, artifacts, inscriptions, escorts, and quest progress that are expensive to reproduce.

**How progress is saved:** Permadeath depends on mode; the character is persisted for continuation, but normal play does not provide arbitrary rollback slots.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a vault, major boss, or late-game dungeon. Restore the exact build after a fatal mistake rather than losing the character permanently.

games.name: XCOM 2
games.info:
**Context:** The **Valhalla** achievement requires finishing on Commander+ in Ironman, so a late squad wipe can waste a long achievement attempt.

**How progress is saved:** Ironman maintains one campaign save and commits tactical casualties and mission results as it advances.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a Chosen/Alien Ruler fight, retaliation, facility assault, or critical tactical turn. Restore after a wipe or veteran loss instead of restarting the Valhalla run.

save.path: {XDG_DATA_HOME}/feral-interactive/XCOM 2 WotC/VFS/Local/my games/XCOM2 War of the Chosen/XComGame/SaveData

games.name: Darkwood
games.info:
**Context:** Nightmare makes death final, while even normal play relies on autosaves rather than free manual rollback.

**How progress is saved:** The current autosave is overwritten as the game advances; Nightmare death ends the playthrough.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a dangerous night defense, Silent Forest/Old Woods expedition, or irreversible story choice. Restore after a fatal night or bad outcome instead of replaying the region.

games.name: Stellaris
games.info:
**Context:** Most Stellaris achievements no longer need Ironman, but **Victorious** specifically requires winning in Ironman Mode.

**How progress is saved:** Ironman keeps one evolving autosave rather than a library of manual rollback saves.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a major war, federation/subject change, crisis decision, or other empire-defining commitment. The clearest payoff is protecting a long **Victorious** attempt from one disastrous branch.

games.name: This War of Mine
games.info:
**Context:** A shelter can depend on a small group of survivors, scarce food/medicine, relationships, and upgrades, while one bad scavenging night can permanently kill a key character.

**How progress is saved:** The game advances through automatic day/night saves rather than unrestricted manual slots.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a dangerous scavenging trip, theft, combat, or critical winter decision. Restore after a death or catastrophic resource loss instead of replaying several days of shelter management.

games.name: Void War
games.info:
**Context:** A promising run can hinge on a specific starship build (weapons, modules, reactor power, crew, wargear and artifacts) that is expensive to recreate after one lost fight.

**How progress is saved:** The active run is autosaved and persistent progression is stored separately; permadeath still ends a run rather than leaving reusable rollback points.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a dangerous encounter, boss, or boarding action. Restore the same ship, crew and build after a fatal fight instead of starting a new galaxy.

games.name: The Council
games.info:
**Context:** Dialogue choices spend limited effort, exploit immunities/vulnerabilities, and can lock in investigation or story outcomes.

**How progress is saved:** The game relies on autosaves/checkpoints rather than unrestricted manual saves.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a major confrontation, expensive skill use, or investigation conclusion. Restore to try another dialogue path without replaying the episode.

games.name: Sunless Sea
games.info:
**Context:** In Unforgiving mode, losing a veteran captain means moving on through the legacy system rather than simply reloading that same life.

**How progress is saved:** The game autosaves on docking; manual saving switches the run out of Unforgiving mode.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a dangerous voyage, zee-monster, or story port. Restore the same captain, ship, officers, and cargo after death instead of accepting succession or abandoning Unforgiving.

games.name: The Long Dark
games.info:
**Context:** A Survival run can represent hundreds of in-game days, stocked bases, crafted clothing, mapped routes, and maxed skills.

**How progress is saved:** Survival autosaves, and death normally ends the run; Cheat Death exists but has limited uses and penalties.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a bear/moose encounter, thin ice, timberwolf territory, or a long blizzard-prone trek. Restore without spending a Cheat Death use or accepting its penalties.

games.name: Enter the Gungeon
games.info:
**Context:** A deep run can have a rare gun/passive synergy, Master Rounds, keys, health, and secret-route progress that is hard to reproduce.

**How progress is saved:** The Save Button serializes the run only at floor exits and resumes on the next floor.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint at a floor exit before a late floor, secret route, or boss sequence. Restore the same build after death instead of rerolling the run.

games.name: Total War: Attila
games.info:
**Context:** ATTILA campaigns can collapse quickly when one lost army or settlement triggers food, public-order, invasion, and migration problems.

**How progress is saved:** Legendary relies on an evolving autosave history rather than free manual rollback.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a Hun battle, exposed-settlement defense, migration, or dangerous End Turn. Restore before the collapse instead of trying to recover from several cascading losses.

games.name: ADOM: Ancient Domains of Mystery
games.info:
**Context:** Traditional-mode characters accumulate artifacts, intrinsics, skills, corruption management, and quest progress that disappear with permadeath.

**How progress is saved:** Traditional mode uses a suspend-style save; Story mode already offers normal save/load and is not the main use case.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a major dungeon branch, vault, boss, or corruption-heavy push. Restore the exact late-game character instead of recreating rare artifacts and trained skills.

games.name: Caves of Qud
games.info:
**Context:** Classic mode can turn one character into a rare mix of mutations/cybernetics, artifacts, reputation, companions, and deep-world progress.

**How progress is saved:** Classic autosaves and supports Save & Quit, but it does not provide unrestricted rollback slots.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a dangerous historic site, deep cave, hostile settlement, or irreversible build experiment. Restore after a death or bad mutation/cybernetic choice without rerolling the character.

games.name: Total War: Shogun 2
games.info:
**Context:** Legendary turns every bad siege, agent loss, or Realm Divide misstep into a committed campaign result after many turns of buildup.

**How progress is saved:** Legendary only exposes the latest automatic campaign state instead of normal manual saves.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before Realm Divide, a decisive siege, or a risky war declaration. Restore after a campaign-breaking loss instead of replaying dozens of turns.

games.name: Europa Universalis V
games.info:
**Context:** EU5 achievements require Ironman, so long achievement setups are exposed to the same one-save commitment as the rest of the campaign.

**How progress is saved:** Ironman keeps one evolving save with no normal manual rollback.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a major war, peace settlement, succession, or achievement-critical decision. Restore after a campaign-breaking outcome instead of rebuilding the run from 1337.

games.name: Battle Brothers
games.info:
**Context:** Battle Brothers has Ironman-specific achievements, while a single bad battle can kill veteran brothers and destroy famed gear built over a long campaign.

**How progress is saved:** Ironman keeps one automatically updated campaign state with no normal pre-battle rollback.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a legendary location, crisis battle, or dangerous contract. Restore after a company-wrecking casualty instead of restarting an Ironman achievement run.

games.name: Barony
games.info:
**Context:** A late dungeon run can carry rare spellbooks, equipment, levels, food, and a strong party composition that disappears on a wipe.

**How progress is saved:** Save & Quit preserves the active run, but permadeath rules do not give you reusable pre-death checkpoints.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint at a floor boundary before a boss or dangerous stretch. A wipe can then be retried with the same party and loot instead of restarting the dungeon.

games.name: Kingdom Come: Deliverance
games.info:
**Context:** Manual saves normally cost **Saviour Schnapps**, making frequent pre-risk saving deliberately inconvenient.

**How progress is saved:** SaveScummer can preserve the same game state externally without consuming another Schnapps.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before stealing, lockpicking, a difficult fight, or a risky dialogue. Retry freely without burning through Schnapps or falling back to an older autosave.

games.name: Hearts of Iron IV
games.info:
**Context:** HOI4 achievement runs require Ironman, and one failed offensive or diplomatic commitment can destroy years of buildup.

**How progress is saved:** Ironman relies on autosaves and exit saves rather than manual branching.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a major offensive, declaration, focus/decision lock-in, or peace conference. Restore after a catastrophic encirclement or bad outcome instead of restarting the achievement campaign.

games.name: Spelunky 2
games.info:
**Context:** The obvious value would be protecting a deep run with rare equipment, quest-chain progress, and access to late-game routes.

**How progress is saved:** The PC game does not normally serialize an active run for Save & Quit; quitting abandons it.

**SaveScummer value:** A file-only SaveScummer cannot reliably preserve the live run, so the useful pre-Olmec or late-route checkpoint requires runtime capture or a mod-created run save.

games.name: Vampyr
games.info:
**Context:** Embracing a named citizen grants major XP but permanently removes that person and can damage an entire district.

**How progress is saved:** The campaign uses one autosave-driven state rather than manual save slots.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before embracing a citizen, resolving a Pillar decision, or making a district-changing quest choice. Restore to compare the power gain against keeping the NPC alive without replaying the chapter.

games.name: Wizard of Legend
games.info:
**Context:** The desired value is protecting a rare arcana/relic build before a Council Member or Sura attempt.

**How progress is saved:** The game does not normally save an active run for later continuation.

**SaveScummer value:** A file-only SaveScummer cannot preserve that live build, so the core use case is unsupported without runtime capture or a mod-created run save.

games.name: Caveblazers
games.info:
**Context:** The useful case would be protecting a strong perk/equipment build before a late cave or boss.

**How progress is saved:** The released game does not normally save and resume an active run.

**SaveScummer value:** A file-only SaveScummer cannot currently deliver that rollback reliably. Keep this candidate only if hands-on testing finds recoverable live-run state.

games.name: State of Decay 2
games.info:
**Context:** A community can contain rare survivors, maxed skills, leader progress, vehicles, weapons, and a developed base, while survivor death is permanent.

**How progress is saved:** The game autosaves the community continuously rather than offering manual rollback slots.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before attacking a Plague Heart, entering a lethal zone, or taking a favorite survivor into a dangerous fight. Restore after a permanent death instead of rebuilding that survivor and their gear.

games.name: Pathologic 2
games.info:
**Context:** Death permanently makes the playthrough harder, and those penalties survive ordinary reloads.

**How progress is saved:** The death penalty is stored beyond the ordinary save being loaded, so SaveScummer must restore that broader state too.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a dangerous fight, infected district, or desperate supply run. Restore after death to undo the persistent penalty that the game's own reload cannot remove.

games.name: Streets of Rogue
games.info:
**Context:** A good run can carry a strong character build, followers, items, money, and mission progress into the later districts.

**How progress is saved:** The game autosaves between levels; resume is coarser than an arbitrary mid-floor quicksave.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a difficult district or risky mission. Restore the previous floor state after a bad outcome instead of rebuilding the whole city run.

games.name: My Summer Car
games.info:
**Context:** Permadeath has its own achievements, including **And it is gone!** for dying with permadeath enabled, while the same save may contain hours of Satsuma work and money progression.

**How progress is saved:** Permadeath can remove the main save on death, so the checkpoint must be taken before the fatal attempt.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before intentionally earning the death achievement, a rally, or another risky drive. Restore afterward and keep the same car/build instead of sacrificing the whole permadeath save.

games.name: Synthetik: Legion Rising
games.info:
**Context:** The desired value is protecting a high-roll weapon/module build before a late stage or boss.

**How progress is saved:** The game does not support saving and resuming an active run.

**SaveScummer value:** A file-only SaveScummer cannot restore the live run, so the useful late-run checkpoint would require runtime capture rather than ordinary save-file versioning.

games.name: Dead Cells
games.info:
**Context:** A promising run may have rare weapon affixes, mutations, scroll scaling, flask charges, and a route you do not want to reroll.

**How progress is saved:** The active run is persisted for Continue, but the game does not keep earlier pre-biome or pre-boss states for rollback.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a boss, risky biome, or major build decision. Restore the exact loadout after death instead of waiting for another run to produce the same synergy.

games.name: Into the Breach
games.info:
**Context:** A campaign can hinge on preserving pilots, Grid health, objectives, and a perfect island while each battle only gives limited correction.

**How progress is saved:** You normally get one Reset Turn per battle, not an unlimited history of earlier turns or pre-mission states.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a difficult island mission or critical turn. Restore after spending Reset Turn and still losing a pilot, objective, or Grid instead of accepting the damaged timeline.

games.name: Total War: Warhammer II
games.info:
**Context:** A Legendary campaign can invest dozens of turns into legendary lords, elite armies, settlements, and campaign objectives before one battle or End Turn cascade destroys them.

**How progress is saved:** Legendary restricts manual saving and maintains the campaign through automatic saves.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a risky siege, confederation, war declaration, or dangerous End Turn. Restore before losing a key lord/army and the turns invested in building it.

games.name: Sunless Skies
games.info:
**Context:** Legacy Mode turns a dead captain into a successor, so a long-developed captain and locomotive are intentionally not restored intact.

**How progress is saved:** The lineage is autosaved around ports/platforms rather than through free manual rollback.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a dangerous reach, terror/fuel crisis, or story expedition. Restore the veteran captain instead of advancing to the successor state.

games.name: Slasher's Keep
games.info:
**Context:** A developed character can carry strong weapons, traits, stats, and inventory into floors where one failed push can undo hours of progress.

**How progress is saved:** The save pedestal / Save & Exit state is mainly for continuation and must be captured before the loss is committed.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint after saving and before a dangerous floor or boss. Restore the same character after a fatal setback instead of rebuilding the loadout.

games.name: Star of Providence
games.info:
**Context:** A strong run can have rare weapons, upgrades, health, and floor progress that are tedious to reproduce.

**How progress is saved:** Continue resumes from a floor-start state rather than the exact room where you quit.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint at the start of a late floor before a boss or difficult section. Restore the same build after death instead of starting from the first area.

games.name: Risk of Rain 2
games.info:
**Context:** A looping run can accumulate hours of survivor-specific items and lunar choices before Mithrix or a Void route.

**How progress is saved:** The game does not natively serialize an active run for Save & Quit.

**SaveScummer value:** A file-only SaveScummer cannot freeze that live run. Protecting a long pre-Mithrix or pre-Void build would require runtime capture rather than save-file backups.

games.name: BattleTech
games.info:
**Context:** The **I Am Iron Man!** achievement requires completing a campaign with Iron Man enabled, where rare Mechs, weapons, pilots, and company finances are all at risk.

**How progress is saved:** Iron Man uses a single campaign save and disables the normal pre/post-mission save history.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a high-skull contract or Priority Mission. Restore after losing a veteran pilot, rare chassis/weapon, or enough money to cripple the achievement run.

games.name: Slay the Spire
games.info:
**Context:** A late deck can contain a rare card/relic engine that may take many runs to see again.

**How progress is saved:** The game autosaves the current run and Save & Quit resumes it, but earlier deck/path states are normally overwritten.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before an Act boss, Elite path, event, shop, or build-defining reward. Restore to retry or compare the decision without rerolling the entire deck.

games.name: Roboquest
games.info:
**Context:** A late run can have a high-roll weapon/perk setup that is expensive to recreate before a difficult biome or boss.

**How progress is saved:** Single-player Save & Quit is available at the end of each level, creating a clean inter-level checkpoint.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint at the end of a level before a difficult late biome or boss. Restore the same build after failure instead of rerolling weapons and perks from the start.

games.name: Cogmind
games.info:
**Context:** A deep run can have a highly specific robot assembled from rare propulsion, weapons, utilities, storage, and route choices.

**How progress is saved:** Normal play saves an unfinished run for continuation; built-in rollback aids depend on mode, so the value is highest where those aids are absent.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a high-security map, risky route, or major rebuild. Restore the exact machine after a disastrous engagement instead of reconstructing its parts and route.

games.name: Wildermyth
games.info:
**Context:** The **Let Me Get My Chisel** achievement requires completing a Carved in Stone campaign, where hero deaths and story outcomes are committed.

**How progress is saved:** Carved in Stone keeps one save and removes the normal Load option.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a chapter climax, risky transformation, or battle involving a key legacy hero. Restore after a permanent loss instead of replaying the whole Carved in Stone campaign.

games.name: Heaven's Vault
games.info:
**Context:** Translations, artifact decisions, destinations, and conversations can close routes or reshape Aliya's interpretation of the mystery.

**How progress is saved:** The game keeps one autosaved narrative state rather than manual branch saves.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before committing to a translation, destination, artifact handoff, or major conversation. Restore to test another interpretation or route without replaying the expedition.

games.name: Total War: Three Kingdoms
games.info:
**Context:** A Legendary campaign ties military progress to named characters, relationships, court positions, coalitions, and territory, so one death or diplomatic break can have long consequences.

**How progress is saved:** Legendary relies on automatic campaign saves instead of unrestricted manual rollback.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a decisive battle, duel-heavy fight, coalition/vassal decision, or risky End Turn. Restore before losing a key character or diplomatic structure.

games.name: Outward
games.info:
**Context:** Defeat can trigger capture, relocation, lost time, lost items, or quest consequences instead of a simple reload.

**How progress is saved:** The game autosaves continuously; current versions expose a limited history of older autosaves rather than unrestricted manual slots.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a dangerous dungeon, timed quest, or expedition with valuable gear. Restore a clean pre-defeat state when the built-in rollback history is too coarse or already overwritten.

games.name: Jupiter Hell
games.info:
**Context:** A late run can have a very specific weapon, perk, armor, and resource setup that is difficult to reproduce after death.

**How progress is saved:** Save & Exit preserves the current run for continuation, not as a history of rollback points.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a difficult branch, boss, or build-defining gamble. If the fight kills the run, restore the same arsenal and perk setup rather than replaying the early moons.

games.name: Imperator: Rome
games.info:
**Context:** Imperator achievement runs use Ironman, where a civil war, succession crisis, or disastrous war can erase decades of state-building.

**How progress is saved:** Ironman continually overwrites a single campaign state.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a major war, civil-war threshold, succession, or high-impact political decision. Restore the realm after a cascade instead of restarting the achievement run.

games.name: Noita
games.info:
**Context:** A long run can contain custom wands, stacked perks, rare spells, parallel-world progress, and hours of irreversible world changes.

**How progress is saved:** Save & Quit persists the whole active world/run across a large save set, so a safe checkpoint needs the complete save state.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before testing a volatile wand, entering a dangerous biome or boss, or starting a parallel-world expedition. Restore after polymorph, self-damage, or another sudden run-ending mistake.

games.name: Six Ages: Ride Like the Wind
games.info:
**Context:** Heroquests, marriages, feuds, raids, and ritual choices can alter clan relationships and resources for years.

**How progress is saved:** The game autosaves whenever the clan state changes rather than exposing manual branch slots.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a heroquest, marriage, raid, or major diplomatic decision. Restore to test another outcome without replaying the intervening seasons.
installDirs: Six Ages Ride Like the Wind

games.name: One Step from Eden
games.info:
**Context:** A late run can have a rare spell/artifact synergy and route that is difficult to rebuild after one failed fight.

**How progress is saved:** The game can save an active run while out of battle, giving SaveScummer a documented between-battle state.

**SaveScummer value:** Checkpoint before a boss, route choice, or ending-critical encounter. Restore the same deck and route after failure instead of rebuilding the combo from scratch.
